issues.description: In the template, PersonService.getAllPersons(PersonSortingOptions) returns a new ArrayList copy of the internal persons list (preserving the internal list), while the solution returns a direct reference to the internal list (this.persons) in some cases and sorts the internal list in-place. This is a structural inconsistency in the API/behavior of getAllPersons: the template implies callers receive an independent copy, whereas the solution mutates and exposes the internal collection. Exposing and sorting the internal list in-place can cause surprising side effects for callers and is inconsistent with the copy-based return in the template. Since the problem text instructs sorting to be implemented in PersonService, students may reasonably expect that getAllPersons returns a safe (non-mutating) collection; the difference between template and solution can confuse students about whether they must or must not mutate the internal list and what the method should return.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the template and solution consistent about the return semantics of getAllPersons. Prefer returning a sorted copy (not the internal list) to avoid side effects: inside PersonService.getAllPersons create a new List<Person> copy = new ArrayList<>(this.persons), sort the copy according to sortingOptions, and return the copy (or an unmodifiable copy). Update both template and solution to follow this approach so students clearly see the intended safe behavior.
